questions.questionText: Which unit is most reasonable for measuring the time it takes to fly between two distant cities?
questions.questionHtml: Which unit is most reasonable for measuring the time it takes to fly between two distant cities?
questions.explanation: A flight between distant cities usually takes several hours. Miles measure distance, gallons measure volume, and milliseconds are far too short for a trip.

questions.questionText: What is the prime factorization of 64?
questions.questionHtml: What is the prime factorization of 64?
questions.explanation: 64 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 2⁶. Every factor must be prime. Although 4³ and 8² also equal 64, their bases are composite.

questions.questionText: What is the value of 0.84 ÷ 0.06?
questions.questionHtml: What is the value of 0.84 ÷ 0.06?
questions.explanation: Multiply both numbers by 100: 0.84 ÷ 0.06 = 84 ÷ 6 = 14. Check: 14 × 0.06 = 0.84.

questions.questionText: What is the value of 3/4 − 1/6 + 2/3?
questions.questionHtml: What is the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math> − <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></math> + <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>?
questions.explanation: Use denominator 12: 9/12 − 2/12 + 8/12 = 15/12 = 1 1/4. Add and subtract the numerators after making the denominators equal.

questions.questionText: Ava has 18 red beads, 30 blue beads, and some yellow beads. She uses all the beads to make identical groups, each with the same number of each color. The greatest possible number of groups is 6. Which could be the number of yellow beads?
questions.questionHtml: Ava has 18 red beads, 30 blue beads, and some yellow beads. She uses all the beads to make identical groups, each with the same number of each color. The greatest possible number of groups is 6. Which could be the number of yellow beads?
questions.explanation: The greatest common factor of 18 and 30 is 6. The yellow count must also be divisible by 6; only 24 works. Each group then has 3 red, 5 blue, and 4 yellow beads.

questions.questionText: One interior angle of a parallelogram is 112°. What is the measure of the adjacent interior angle x?
questions.questionHtml: One interior angle of a parallelogram is 112°. What is the measure of the adjacent interior angle x?<svg class="review-diagram" viewBox="0 0 340 175" role="img" aria-label="A parallelogram with adjacent interior angles 112 degrees and x degrees"><polygon points="40,145 80,45 300,45 260,145" fill="#eaf1ff" stroke="#173957" stroke-width="2"/><text x="94" y="75">112°</text><text x="261" y="75">x°</text></svg>
questions.explanation: Adjacent interior angles of a parallelogram add to 180°. Therefore x = 180° − 112° = 68°. Opposite angles are equal, but these two angles are adjacent.

questions.questionText: Which fact is enough to prove that a quadrilateral is a rectangle?
questions.questionHtml: Which fact is enough to prove that a quadrilateral is a rectangle?

options.label: A
options.text: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
options.html: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.

options.label: B
options.text: Both pairs of opposite sides have equal lengths.
options.html: Both pairs of opposite sides have equal lengths.

options.label: C
options.text: All four sides have equal lengths.
options.html: All four sides have equal lengths.

options.label: D
options.text: All four interior angles have equal measures.
options.html: All four interior angles have equal measures.

questions.correctAnswer: All four interior angles have equal measures.
questions.correctHtml: All four interior angles have equal measures.
questions.explanation: The interior angles of a quadrilateral add to 360°. If all four are equal, each is 90°, so the figure is a rectangle. Equal or parallel opposite sides alone only prove a parallelogram.

questions.questionText: A pizza is cut into 24 equal slices. Mia eats 1/3 of the pizza. Noah then eats 1/4 of the slices that remain. Eli eats all the slices left after Noah. How many slices does Eli eat?
questions.questionHtml: A pizza is cut into 24 equal slices. Mia eats <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math> of the pizza. Noah then eats <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math> of the slices that remain. Eli eats all the slices left after Noah. How many slices does Eli eat?
questions.explanation: Mia eats 24 ÷ 3 = 8 slices, leaving 16. Noah eats 16 ÷ 4 = 4 of those remaining slices. Eli eats 16 − 4 = 12 slices. The second fraction applies to the remainder, not the original pizza.

questions.questionText: Two walls each measure 2 yards by 4 yards. Two other walls each measure 4 yards by 4 yards. Six identical rolls of wallpaper cover all four walls with no waste. How many square feet does one roll cover? (1 yard = 3 feet.)
questions.questionHtml: Two walls each measure 2 yards by 4 yards. Two other walls each measure 4 yards by 4 yards. Six identical rolls of wallpaper cover all four walls with no waste. How many square feet does one roll cover? (1 yard = 3 feet.)
questions.explanation: Total area = 2 × (2 × 4) + 2 × (4 × 4) = 48 square yards. A square yard is 3 × 3 = 9 square feet, so the walls cover 432 square feet. Each roll covers 432 ÷ 6 = 72 square feet.

questions.questionText: A smaller cube has side length 2 cm, and a larger cube has side length 3 cm. What is the ratio of the smaller cube’s volume to the larger cube’s volume?
questions.questionHtml: A smaller cube has side length 2 cm, and a larger cube has side length 3 cm. What is the ratio of the smaller cube’s volume to the larger cube’s volume?
questions.explanation: Cube each side length: 2³ = 8 cm³ and 3³ = 27 cm³. The volume ratio is 8:27. A side-length ratio of 2:3 is not the volume ratio.

questions.questionText: A building is 24.5 meters tall, and a tree is 3 1/2 meters tall. The building is how many times as tall as the tree?
questions.questionHtml: A building is 24.5 meters tall, and a tree is 3 <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> meters tall. The building is how many times as tall as the tree?
questions.explanation: Convert 3 1/2 to 3.5. Then 24.5 ÷ 3.5 = 245 ÷ 35 = 7. The building is 7 times as tall as the tree. Check: 3.5 × 7 = 24.5.

questions.questionText: Of 360 trees on a farm, 5/6 are orange trees. Of the orange trees, 1/5 did not bloom this year. How many orange trees bloomed?
questions.questionHtml: Of 360 trees on a farm, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></math> are orange trees. Of the orange trees, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math> did not bloom this year. How many orange trees bloomed?
questions.explanation: First find the orange trees: 360 × 5/6 = 300. Then 300 ÷ 5 = 60 did not bloom. The number that bloomed is 300 − 60 = 240. The second fraction applies only to the orange trees.

questions.questionText: Nora spends 1/4 of her money on a notebook. She then spends 2/5 of her remaining money on pens. What fraction of her original money is left?
questions.questionHtml: Nora spends <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math> of her money on a notebook. She then spends <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math> of her remaining money on pens. What fraction of her original money is left?
questions.explanation: Nora has 3/4 left after buying the notebook. She then keeps 3/5 of that remainder, so 3/4 × 3/5 = 9/20 of her original money is left. Do not subtract 2/5 from the original whole.

questions.questionText: A square has side length b. An isosceles right triangle with legs of length 6a is cut from one corner, as shown. Which expression gives the area of the shaded region that remains?
questions.questionHtml: A square has side length b. An isosceles right triangle with legs of length 6a is cut from one corner, as shown. Which expression gives the area of the shaded region that remains?<svg class="review-diagram" viewBox="0 0 320 230" role="img" aria-label="A square with side b. A right triangle with equal legs 6a is removed from the top left corner. The remaining region is shaded."><polygon points="150,40 230,40 230,200 70,200 70,120" fill="#e3f7ef"/><rect x="70" y="40" width="160" height="160" fill="none" stroke="#173957" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M150 40 L70 120" fill="none" stroke="#173957" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><text x="240" y="125">b</text><text x="102" y="29">6a</text><text x="35" y="85">6a</text></svg>
questions.explanation: The square has area b². The removed right triangle has area 1/2 × 6a × 6a = 18a². The remaining area is b² − 18a². Multiplying the legs without dividing by 2 would remove twice the triangle’s area.

questions.questionText: A large cube has side length 18 feet. It is completely filled, with no gaps, by 27 identical smaller cubes arranged in rows and layers. What is the side length of each smaller cube?
questions.questionHtml: A large cube has side length 18 feet. It is completely filled, with no gaps, by 27 identical smaller cubes arranged in rows and layers. What is the side length of each smaller cube?
questions.explanation: 27 = 3 × 3 × 3, so there are 3 small cubes along each edge. Divide the large edge by 3: 18 ÷ 3 = 6 feet. Check with volumes: 27 × 6³ = 5,832 cubic feet, the same as 18³.

questions.questionText: A rectangular prism is built from small cubes. It is 6 cubes long, 2 cubes wide, and 3 cubes high. Each small cube has volume 2 cm³. What is the total volume of the prism?
questions.questionHtml: A rectangular prism is built from small cubes. It is 6 cubes long, 2 cubes wide, and 3 cubes high. Each small cube has volume 2 cm³. What is the total volume of the prism?
questions.explanation: The prism contains 6 × 2 × 3 = 36 small cubes. Each cube has volume 2 cm³, so the total is 36 × 2 = 72 cm³. Counting cubes is the first step; multiplying by each cube’s volume is the second.

questions.questionText: What is the prime factorization of 125?
questions.questionHtml: What is the prime factorization of 125?
questions.explanation: 125 = 5 × 5 × 5 = 5³. Every factor is prime. The product 25 × 5 equals 125, but 25 is not prime, so the factorization is not finished.

questions.questionText: A building is 18.75 meters tall, and a tree is 2 1/2 meters tall. The building is how many times as tall as the tree?
questions.questionHtml: A building is 18.75 meters tall, and a tree is 2 <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> meters tall. The building is how many times as tall as the tree?

questions.questionText: Of 240 trees on a farm, 3/4 are pear trees. Of the pear trees, 1/6 did not bloom this year. How many pear trees bloomed?
questions.questionHtml: Of 240 trees on a farm, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math> are pear trees. Of the pear trees, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></math> did not bloom this year. How many pear trees bloomed?
questions.explanation: There are 240 × 3/4 = 180 pear trees. Of those, 180 ÷ 6 = 30 did not bloom. Therefore 180 − 30 = 150 pear trees bloomed.

questions.questionText: Leo spends 2/5 of his money on a book. He then spends 1/3 of his remaining money on a game. What fraction of his original money is left?
questions.questionHtml: Leo spends <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math> of his money on a book. He then spends <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math> of his remaining money on a game. What fraction of his original money is left?
questions.explanation: After buying the book, Leo has 3/5 left. He keeps 2/3 of that remainder after buying the game. So he has 3/5 × 2/3 = 2/5 of his original money left.

questions.questionText: A square has side length b. An isosceles right triangle with legs of length 4a is cut from one corner, as shown. Which expression gives the area of the shaded region that remains?
questions.questionHtml: A square has side length b. An isosceles right triangle with legs of length 4a is cut from one corner, as shown. Which expression gives the area of the shaded region that remains?<svg class="review-diagram" viewBox="0 0 320 230" role="img" aria-label="A square with side b. A right triangle with equal legs 4a is removed from the top left corner. The remaining region is shaded."><polygon points="150,40 230,40 230,200 70,200 70,120" fill="#e3f7ef"/><rect x="70" y="40" width="160" height="160" fill="none" stroke="#173957" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M150 40 L70 120" fill="none" stroke="#173957" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><text x="240" y="125">b</text><text x="102" y="29">4a</text><text x="35" y="85">4a</text></svg>
questions.explanation: The square’s area is b². The triangle’s area is 1/2 × 4a × 4a = 8a². Subtract the removed triangle: b² − 8a². Remember the 1/2 in the triangle-area formula.

questions.questionText: A large cube has side length 12 cm. It is completely filled, with no gaps, by 216 identical smaller cubes arranged in rows and layers. What is the side length of each smaller cube?
questions.questionHtml: A large cube has side length 12 cm. It is completely filled, with no gaps, by 216 identical smaller cubes arranged in rows and layers. What is the side length of each smaller cube?
questions.explanation: 216 = 6 × 6 × 6, so there are 6 small cubes along each edge. Each small cube has side length 12 ÷ 6 = 2 cm. Check: the large volume is 1,728 cm³; 216 × 2³ = 1,728 cm³.

questions.questionText: A rectangular prism is built from small cubes. It is 5 cubes long, 3 cubes wide, and 2 cubes high. Each small cube has volume 1.5 cm³. What is the total volume of the prism?
questions.questionHtml: A rectangular prism is built from small cubes. It is 5 cubes long, 3 cubes wide, and 2 cubes high. Each small cube has volume 1.5 cm³. What is the total volume of the prism?
questions.explanation: Count the small cubes: 5 × 3 × 2 = 30. Multiply by the volume of each cube: 30 × 1.5 = 45 cm³. Do not confuse the number of cubes with the volume.

questions.questionText: A pizza is cut into 36 equal slices. Lena eats 1/4 of the pizza. Owen then eats 1/3 of the slices that remain. How many slices are left after both have eaten?
questions.questionHtml: A pizza is cut into 36 equal slices. Lena eats <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math> of the pizza. Owen then eats <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math> of the slices that remain. How many slices are left after both have eaten?
questions.explanation: Lena eats 36 ÷ 4 = 9 slices, leaving 27. Owen eats 27 ÷ 3 = 9 slices. There are 27 − 9 = 18 slices left. Each step uses the amount left at that point.

questions.questionText: Two walls each measure 2 yards by 3 yards. Two other walls each measure 5 yards by 3 yards. Six identical rolls of wallpaper cover all four walls with no waste. How many square feet does one roll cover? (1 yard = 3 feet.)
questions.questionHtml: Two walls each measure 2 yards by 3 yards. Two other walls each measure 5 yards by 3 yards. Six identical rolls of wallpaper cover all four walls with no waste. How many square feet does one roll cover? (1 yard = 3 feet.)
questions.explanation: Total area = 2 × (2 × 3) + 2 × (5 × 3) = 42 square yards. Convert area by multiplying by 9: 42 × 9 = 378 square feet. Each roll covers 378 ÷ 6 = 63 square feet.

questions.questionText: A smaller cube has side length 3 inches, and a larger cube has side length 4 inches. What is the ratio of the smaller cube’s volume to the larger cube’s volume?
questions.questionHtml: A smaller cube has side length 3 inches, and a larger cube has side length 4 inches. What is the ratio of the smaller cube’s volume to the larger cube’s volume?
questions.explanation: The volumes are 3³ = 27 cubic inches and 4³ = 64 cubic inches. Write smaller to larger in the requested order: 27:64.

questions.questionText: A bus travels 240 miles between two cities. Which unit is most reasonable for measuring the time the trip takes?
questions.questionHtml: A bus travels 240 miles between two cities. Which unit is most reasonable for measuring the time the trip takes?
questions.explanation: Use hours to measure the time taken by a long bus trip. Miles measure the distance traveled, not the time. Pounds measure weight, and milliseconds are far too short for this trip.

questions.questionText: What is the value of 0.96 ÷ 0.08?
questions.questionHtml: What is the value of 0.96 ÷ 0.08?
questions.explanation: Multiply both numbers by 100: 0.96 ÷ 0.08 = 96 ÷ 8 = 12. Multiplying both by the same number leaves the quotient unchanged. Check: 12 × 0.08 = 0.96.

questions.questionText: What is the value of 7/8 − 1/6 + 5/12?
questions.questionHtml: What is the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></math> − <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></math> + <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac></math>?

questions.questionText: Ben has 24 red counters, 36 blue counters, and some yellow counters. He uses all the counters to make identical groups, each with the same number of each color. The greatest possible number of groups is 12. Which could be the number of yellow counters?
questions.questionHtml: Ben has 24 red counters, 36 blue counters, and some yellow counters. He uses all the counters to make identical groups, each with the same number of each color. The greatest possible number of groups is 12. Which could be the number of yellow counters?
questions.explanation: The greatest common factor of 24 and 36 is 12. The yellow count must also be divisible by 12; only 48 works. Twelve groups then have 2 red, 3 blue, and 4 yellow counters each.

questions.questionText: One interior angle of a parallelogram is 118°. What is the measure of the adjacent interior angle x?
questions.questionHtml: One interior angle of a parallelogram is 118°. What is the measure of the adjacent interior angle x?<svg class="review-diagram" viewBox="0 0 340 175" role="img" aria-label="A parallelogram with adjacent interior angles 118 degrees and x degrees"><polygon points="40,145 93,45 300,45 247,145" fill="#eaf1ff" stroke="#173957" stroke-width="2"/><text x="107" y="75">118°</text><text x="261" y="75">x°</text></svg>
questions.explanation: Adjacent interior angles in a parallelogram add to 180°. Therefore x = 180° − 118° = 62°. Equal opposite angles are a different relationship from adjacent angles.

questions.questionText: Which set of interior angle measures guarantees that a quadrilateral is a rectangle?
questions.questionHtml: Which set of interior angle measures guarantees that a quadrilateral is a rectangle?
questions.explanation: A rectangle must have four right angles, so all four interior angles must be 90°. The other sets each add to 360°, but none has four right angles. A total of 360° alone does not prove a rectangle.

questions.questionText: The block circle, triangle, square, star repeats in that order, starting at position 1. Which shape is at position 47?
questions.questionHtml:
The block circle, triangle, square, star repeats in that order, starting at position 1.

Which shape is at position 47?
questions.explanation: There are 4 shapes in each block. (47 − 1) ÷ 4 leaves remainder 2, so position 47 is the square in position 3 of its block.

questions.questionText: The six-number block 2, 5, 1, 8, 4, 7 repeats in that order, starting at position 1. What is the sum of the numbers at positions 29 and 34?
questions.questionHtml: The six-number block 2, 5, 1, 8, 4, 7 repeats in that order, starting at position 1. What is the sum of the numbers at positions 29 and 34?
questions.explanation: The positions within each block are 5 and 4. Those entries are 4 and 8; their sum is 12.

questions.questionText: If m + 17 = n − 12, what is n − m?
questions.questionHtml: If m + 17 = n − 12, what is n − m?
questions.explanation: Add 12 to both sides and subtract m: n − m = 17 + 12 = 29.

questions.questionText: If 2c + 6d = 18, which expression equals c?
questions.questionHtml: If 2c + 6d = 18, which expression equals c?
questions.explanation: Subtract 6d and divide every term by 2: c = (18 − 6d)/2 = 9 − 3d.

questions.questionText: A tower is 3 times as tall as a pole. The tower's height is (3x + 15) meters. Which expression gives the pole's height in meters?
questions.questionHtml: A tower is 3 times as tall as a pole. The tower's height is (3x + 15) meters. Which expression gives the pole's height in meters?
questions.explanation: Divide the entire tower height by 3: (3x + 15)/3 = x + 5.

questions.questionText: Mia has a stickers. Noah has 2 times as many stickers as Mia. Leo has 5 more stickers than Noah. Which expression does NOT give their total number of stickers?
questions.questionHtml: Mia has a stickers. Noah has 2 times as many stickers as Mia. Leo has 5 more stickers than Noah. Which expression does NOT give their total number of stickers?
questions.explanation: Their total is a + 2a + (2a + 5) = 5a + 5. The expression a + 2(2a + 5) adds the extra 5 twice.

questions.questionText: A call costs $5.00 for the first 4 minutes and $0.35 for each additional minute. For a call lasting m minutes, where m > 4, which equation gives the total cost C in dollars?
questions.questionHtml: A call costs $5.00 for the first 4 minutes and $0.35 for each additional minute. For a call lasting m minutes, where m > 4, which equation gives the total cost C in dollars?
questions.explanation: The first 4 minutes are already included in $5.00. Charge $0.35 for only the remaining m − 4 minutes, then add the initial cost.

questions.questionText: A purse contains only nickels (5 cents) and dimes (10 cents). There are 2 more nickels than dimes, and the total value is $1.00. If d is the number of dimes, which equation models this in cents?
questions.questionHtml: A purse contains only nickels (5 cents) and dimes (10 cents). There are 2 more nickels than dimes, and the total value is $1.00. If d is the number of dimes, which equation models this in cents?
questions.explanation: There are d dimes and d + 2 nickels. Their values in cents are 10d and 5(d + 2); together these equal 100 cents.

questions.questionText: Define m ◆ n = (4 × m) ÷ n. What is 6 ◆ 6?
questions.questionHtml: Define m ◆ n = (4 × m) ÷ n. What is 6 ◆ 6?
questions.explanation: Substitute m = 6 and n = 6 into the definition: (4 × 6) ÷ 6 = 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

questions.questionText: Define F(x) = 5 + (3/2)x. If F(y) = 14, what is y?
questions.questionHtml: Define F(x) = 5 + (3/2)x. If F(y) = 14, what is y?
questions.explanation: Subtract 5 to get (3/2)y = 9. Multiply by 2/3: y = 6. Check: 5 + (3/2) × 6 = 14.

questions.questionText: A rectangle has perimeter 32 centimeters. Quantity A: the area of the rectangle in square centimeters. Quantity B: 64. Compare the quantities.
questions.questionHtml:
A rectangle has perimeter 32 centimeters.

Compare the quantities
Quantity AQuantity B
the area of the rectangle in square centimeters64
questions.explanation: A 8 by 8 square has area 64. A 7 by 9 rectangle has the same perimeter and area 63. Quantity A can equal Quantity B or be smaller, so one relationship cannot be determined.

questions.questionText: BA is perpendicular to BC. The two angles x and y together fill angle ABC. Quantity A: x + 12. Quantity B: 102 − y. Compare the quantities.
questions.questionHtml:
BA is perpendicular to BC. The two angles x and y together fill angle ABC.

Compare the quantities
Quantity AQuantity B
x + 12102 − y
questions.explanation: The right angle gives x + y = 90, so x = 90 − y. Adding 12 gives x + 12 = 102 − y. The quantities are equal.

questions.questionText: An equilateral triangle has side length 5 cm and an interior angle x°. A rhombus has side length 7 cm and an interior angle y°. No angle measure of the rhombus is given. Quantity A: x. Quantity B: y. Compare the quantities.
questions.questionHtml:
An equilateral triangle has side length 5 cm and an interior angle x°. A rhombus has side length 7 cm and an interior angle y°. No angle measure of the rhombus is given.

Compare the quantities
Quantity AQuantity B
xy
questions.explanation: The equilateral triangle gives x = 60°. Equal sides in a rhombus do not determine its angles: y could be 45°, 60°, or 80°, for example. The relationship cannot be determined.

questions.questionText: A parallelogram has area 32 cm² and base 8 cm. Its side of length x cm is slanted, not perpendicular to the base. Quantity A: x. Quantity B: 4. Compare the quantities.
questions.questionHtml:
A parallelogram has area 32 cm² and base 8 cm. Its side of length x cm is slanted, not perpendicular to the base.

Compare the quantities
Quantity AQuantity B
x4
questions.explanation: The perpendicular height is area ÷ base = 32 ÷ 8 = 4 cm. The slanted side x is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with height 4, so x is greater than 4.

questions.questionText: The median age of 18 workers is 34 years. No worker is exactly 34 years old. How many workers are older than 34?
questions.questionHtml: The median age of 18 workers is 34 years. No worker is exactly 34 years old. How many workers are older than 34?
questions.explanation: With 18 ages in order, the median lies between the two middle ages. Since nobody is 34, exactly half are below 34 and half are above: 18 ÷ 2 = 9 workers.

questions.questionText: A list of 10 numbers has mean 24. The sum of the largest 8 numbers is 220. What is the sum of the two smallest numbers?
questions.questionHtml: A list of 10 numbers has mean 24. The sum of the largest 8 numbers is 220. What is the sum of the two smallest numbers?
questions.explanation: The total of all 10 numbers is 10 × 24 = 240. Subtract the largest 8 numbers: 240 − 220 = 20.

questions.skill: Finding a missing value from the mean
questions.questionText: Three students have a mean height of 59 inches. The shortest is 54 inches and the tallest is 64 inches. How tall is the third student?
questions.questionHtml: Three students have a mean height of 59 inches. The shortest is 54 inches and the tallest is 64 inches. How tall is the third student?
questions.explanation: Their total height is 59 × 3 = 177. Subtract the shortest and tallest: 177 − 54 − 64 = 59 inches.

questions.questionText: What is the median of this data set: 18, 10, 13, 25, 15, 11, 16, 22?
questions.questionHtml: What is the median of this data set: 18, 10, 13, 25, 15, 11, 16, 22?
questions.explanation: In order: 10, 11, 13, 15, 16, 18, 22, 25. With 8 values, average the 4th and 5th: (15 + 16) ÷ 2 = 15.5.

questions.questionText: The table records books read by students. One student's entry is corrected from 1 books to 2 books. Which statistics change: mean, median, mode, or range?

options.text: The mean, median, and mode change.
options.html: The mean, median, and mode change.

questions.explanation: The total rises by 1 while the number of students stays 16, so the mean rises. The middle values and most frequent value remain 2. The minimum 0 and maximum 4 remain, so the range stays 4.

questions.explanation: The median and mode are both 26. The mean is 27, greater than the range 9. March plus April is 52. Q1 = 25.5 and Q3 = 28, so the interquartile range is 2.5, not 3.

questions.explanation: The mode is the value with the greatest frequency. 9 players scored 2 goals, more players than for any other goal count. Therefore the mode is 2 goals.

questions.questionText: The scatter plot shows temperature and cups of lemonade sold on six days. Which conclusion is best supported? Data (°F, cups): (52, 14), (56, 22), (60, 26), (64, 34), (68, 38), (72, 46).
questions.questionHtml: The scatter plot shows temperature and cups of lemonade sold on six days. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.label: A
options.text: Exactly the same number of cups was sold each day.
options.html: Exactly the same number of cups was sold each day.

options.label: B
options.text: The plot proves that temperature is the only factor affecting sales.
options.html: The plot proves that temperature is the only factor affecting sales.

options.label: C
options.text: On these days, higher temperatures tended to go with more cups sold.
options.html: On these days, higher temperatures tended to go with more cups sold.

options.label: D
options.text: On these days, higher temperatures tended to go with fewer cups sold.
options.html: On these days, higher temperatures tended to go with fewer cups sold.

questions.correctAnswer: On these days, higher temperatures tended to go with more cups sold.
questions.correctHtml: On these days, higher temperatures tended to go with more cups sold.
questions.explanation: Reading from lower to higher temperatures, the points generally move up, showing a positive association. A scatter plot shows a pattern in these data; it does not prove that temperature alone causes sales.

questions.questionText: The mean weight of the dogs at a shelter is 36 pounds, and the mean weight of the cats is 12 pounds. There is at least one of each, but their counts are not given. Quantity A: the mean weight of all the dogs and cats combined. Quantity B: 24. Compare the quantities.
questions.questionHtml:
The mean weight of the dogs at a shelter is 36 pounds, and the mean weight of the cats is 12 pounds. There is at least one of each, but their counts are not given.

Compare the quantities
Quantity AQuantity B
the mean weight of all the dogs and cats combined24
questions.explanation: Equal numbers would give 24 pounds. More dogs would raise the combined mean; more cats would lower it. Without their counts, the relationship cannot be determined.

questions.questionText: A bucket contains red and blue balls. Each ball is equally likely to be selected. The probability of selecting a red ball is exactly 4/13. Quantity A: the total number of balls in the bucket. Quantity B: 11. Compare the quantities.
questions.questionHtml:
A bucket contains red and blue balls. Each ball is equally likely to be selected. The probability of selecting a red ball is exactly 4/13.

Compare the quantities
Quantity AQuantity B
the total number of balls in the bucket11
questions.explanation: The fraction 4/13 is in lowest terms. A whole-number count requires the total to be a positive multiple of 13, so it is at least 13, greater than 11.

questions.questionText: The youngest person in a group is 18 years old. Nora is 58 years old and is in the group. No other ages are given. Quantity A: the range of ages in the group. Quantity B: 40. Compare the quantities.

questions.explanation: If Nora is oldest, the range is 40. If someone is older than Nora, the range is larger. Quantity A could equal Quantity B or be greater, so the relationship cannot be determined.
